s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless facial swelling with bony expansion
salient_findings: 3-month history of painless swelling in the right upper posterior tooth region
4.0×3.5 cm diffuse, well-defined, hard, nontender swelling on the right middle third of the face
Ground-glass trabecular pattern with radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars on radiographs
key_facts: 9-year-old boy presented with a facial swelling
Swelling is located in the right upper posterior tooth region
Swelling has grown progressively over 3 months
Swelling is painless
Facial asymmetry is present
Medical and family histories are unremarkable
Swelling is 4.0×3.5 cm in size
Swelling is hard and nontender
Overlying skin is normal
Intraoral swelling is present in the right buccal vestibule
Buccal cortical expansion and slight palatal expansion are present
Mucosal changes are absent
Radiographs show a ground-glass trabecular pattern
Radiolucency is present around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars

shortlist.label: Juvenile ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical and radiological findings of a progressive, painless facial swelling with bony expansion and a ground-glass trabecular pattern

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a ground-glass appearance, although the well-defined margin makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Possible due to the presence of a painless facial swelling with bony expansion, although the age and location are not typical

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible due to the presence of a jaw swelling with radiolucency around the roots of teeth, although the absence of pain and the ground-glass pattern are not typical

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible due to the presence of a painless jaw swelling with bony expansion and a ground-glass appearance, although the location and age are not typical

raw.rationale: The well-defined margin of the swelling and the ground-glass internal pattern on imaging are consistent with juvenile ossifying fibroma, and the presence of radiolucency around the roots of deciduous teeth and erupting premolars also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Ill-defined margin and merging with surrounding areas are characteristic of fibrous dysplasia, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Typically presents with bilateral involvement and familial history, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Usually presents with more aggressive features and radiolucency, which is not consistent with the ground-glass appearance seen in this case

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more mixed radiolucent and radiopaque appearance, which is not consistent with the ground-glass pattern seen in this case
